items.question: What does it print?

options.why: The parameters have no `&`, so `swap_px` swaps its own copies and the caller's `bid` and `ask` never change.
Passing `double`s by value is legal. It just does nothing useful here.

feedback.correct: The swap happened to the copies.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Are `a` and `b` the caller's variables, or copies?

explain.text: `a` and `b` are copies of `bid` and `ask`, swapped and then destroyed at the `}`. The caller's variables keep 99.5 and 100.5. `double& a, double& b` would swap them.

items.question: Inside `void report(const std::vector<double>& v)`, select all that apply: which lines compile?

options.why: `push_back` changes the vector, and `v` is a `const` reference, so it is rejected.

feedback.correct: Read `v`, or change your own copy.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Which lines change `v` itself?

explain.text: Reading through `v` is allowed, and so is copying it into a vector of your own and changing that. Only `v.push_back` writes through the `const` reference, so only it is rejected.

items.question: `struct Level { double px; long long size; };` takes 16 bytes. `const Level* p` holds 0x4000. How many bytes past 0x4000 is the address `p + 5`?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Multiply the steps by the size of one `Level`.

byKey.five: You counted elements. Each step moves a whole 16-byte `Level`.
byKey.eight: You used 8 bytes per step. A `Level` holds a `double` and a `long long`: 16 bytes.

explain.text: Pointer arithmetic moves whole objects: `p + 5` is 5 × 16 = 80 bytes on, address 0x4050. That is why `++p` walks an array of structs one element at a time.

items.question: Select all that apply: which snippets are undefined behaviour?

options.text: `double* f() { double x = 1.0; return &x; }` then reading `*f()`
`double* p = new double(1.0); delete p; delete p;`

options.why: Allocating zero elements is legal, and freeing the block with `delete[]` is exactly right.
`at` checks the index and throws `std::out_of_range`. That is defined behaviour, a reported error.

feedback.correct: A dead local and a double delete.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Separate checked errors from unchecked ones.

explain.text: Reading a dead local and deleting twice are undefined: this browser build ran both silently. A desk build with `-fsanitize=address` reports "double-free". `new double[0]` is legal, and `v.at(5)` throws a defined exception.

items.question: How many frames are on the stack at the deepest point of `main` calling `depth(4)`, counting `main`?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. List every call that is still waiting when `depth(0)` runs.

byKey.five: You left out `main`, whose frame is at the bottom the whole time.
byKey.four: `depth(0)` is a call too, with its own frame.

explain.text: While `depth(0)` runs, `depth(4)`, `depth(3)`, `depth(2)` and `depth(1)` are waiting, and `main` is under them all: 6 frames. Each returns in reverse order.

items.question: What does it print?

options.why: `book` owns the position and dies at the inner `}`, so the destructor runs before `end`.
`book` is a vector of `unique_ptr`s; when it dies, each owner deletes its position.

feedback.correct: The owner died at the inner brace.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. When does `book` go out of scope?

explain.text: `book` lives inside the braces. At the `}` the vector is destroyed, its `unique_ptr` deletes the position, and `close AZN` prints. Only then does `end` print.

items.prose: A small balance book earns interest once per period.
items.question: Write `accrue(balances, rates)`: change each balance in place; never change or copy the rates.

widget.starter:
#include <vector>

// add one period's interest to each balance: balances[i] *= 1 + rates[i]
widget.how: The first Check downloads the C++ compiler (about 26 MB) and compiles in 10 to 15 s. Later Checks take 1 to 3 s. Check runs 4 hidden tests. Each builds `b`, calls `accrue`, and reads `b` afterwards. Some pass the rates as a temporary `{...}`, which only a `const&` accepts.

feedback.correct: Changed in place, read in place.
feedback.generic: Not yet. The results under the editor say which test failed.

explain.text: `balances` must reach the caller, so it is `std::vector<double>&`. `rates` is only read, and the tests pass it as a temporary, so it must be `const std::vector<double>&`. Two periods at 10% give 121.

options.why: `add` changes the book, so it cannot promise not to. The `const` on its parameter is about `o`, not the book.
Cancelling removes an order, which changes the book.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Which method only reads the book?

explain.text: `best_bid()` only reads, so mark it `double best_bid() const;`. Then code holding a `const Book&`, such as a pricer, can call it.
